relevance_note: The paper studies named patients with familial LCAT deficiency: "The HDL of three patients with familial LCAT deficiency (A. A., A. R., M. R.)"; no LCAT variant is printed (1971, pre-molecular).
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; no script transcribed tables (the script only assembled JSON and checked spans). In-scope people: A. R. and A. A. (the two studied patients) and M. R. (sister of A. R., also called a patient with familial LCAT deficiency, with individual HDL values from unpublished experiments). No gene or variant is named anywhere, so the variants table is empty. Six normal female controls and 16 other normal females are out of scope and get no rows; cohort_size_as_stated counts only the two patients studied. The paper prints no publication year (only received dates, 1970), so year is null. Ages 36 and 42 yr are ages at the time of study, recorded as age at last evaluation. The general disease description in the Introduction (corneal infiltration, anemia, proteinuria) is not attributed to any of these individuals and was not used. Most phenotype rows are lipoprotein composition abnormalities from A. A.'s plasma on or before a low-fat diet; the checklist items 'elevated unesterified (free) cholesterol' and 'reduced cholesteryl ester fraction' were marked observed for A. A. from lipoprotein (HDL subfraction) composition statements, not plasma concentrations. 'Low hdl cholesterol' and 'low ldl cholesterol or apolipoprotein b' were left not reported because the paper reports low HDL protein and low LDL protein concentrations, not cholesterol or apoB; 'hypertriglyceridemia' left not reported because only 'hyperlipemia' and a marked fall of plasma triglycerides on diet are stated. The Discussion text is out of order in the conversion (a fragment beginning 'diet. The concentration of HDL protein...' follows the reference list); it is attributed to A. A. because it concerns the low-fat diet only she received and names her in the same paragraph. Table numbers (Tables II-IV) were not used to derive features by comparison with control values. No internal contradictions found.
